name: Sweet Chariot Poker
description: Sweet Chariot is a lowball variant of Swingo Poker. Players receive five cards, choose two as hole cards and three as board cards, then use their board cards plus one shared river card and one card from any opponent's board to make their best five-card hand. The lowest hand wins the pot. Played with blinds and pot limit betting.

history.origins: Swingo Poker was invented by Steve Albini in December 2007 and developed by the Alliance-X poker group in Chicago; it is named after a song by Naked Raygun. Sweet Chariot is a lowball variation of Swingo: same structure but the lowest hand wins at showdown.
timeline: Thereafter: Sweet Chariot played as lowball variant of Swingo.
history.cultural: Developed in Chicago poker circles; reflects home-game variant culture of shared-card poker.
history.evolution: Sweet Chariot inverts Swingo's showdown: lowest hand wins instead of highest, using the same shared-card and borrow-one-opponent-board-card structure.

setup.players: Two to eight players; best with five to eight.
setup.dealing: Small blind by player to dealer's left, big blind by the next player (twice small). Dealer shuffles and deals five cards face down to each player. First betting round; then each player chooses two hole cards and three board cards; all expose board cards. Second betting round. Dealer deals one shared river card face up to the centre. Third betting round. Showdown: lowest hand wins.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips. Stakes (blinds and pot limit) agreed before play.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the lowest five-card hand at showdown, or by being the last player left after all others fold. Hands are made from two hole cards, three board cards, the river card, and any one card from another player's board.
rules.gameplay: Deal five cards to each player. First betting round (left of big blind). Each player selects two hole cards (hidden) and three board cards (exposed). Second betting round, begun by the player with the highest-ranking board (pairs and trips count; ties broken by suit order clubs low to spades high). Dealer deals one river card face up. Third betting round. Showdown: each player makes the best low hand from seven cards (two hole, three board, river, one from any opponent's board). Lowest hand wins; ties split the pot. A player may not fold if they have already matched the current bet (others may need their board card).
keyRules: Standard 52 cards; no jokers. Blinds and pot limit betting.
Five cards each; two chosen as hole cards, three as board cards (exposed).
One shared river card after second betting round.
Best low hand from seven cards: two hole, three board, river, plus any one card from another player's board.
Lowest hand wins (ace-to-five low ranking). Ace is low; straights and flushes do not count.
Player may not fold when they have already called the current bet.
Board cards must remain visible at showdown even if a player mucks hole cards.

strategy.basic: Aim for five unpaired low cards. Remember opponents can use one of your board cards; avoid exposing cards that complete strong lows for others. Position matters for betting.
strategy.intermediate: Track which board cards help which opponents. Bet to force folds and remove a key board card from the table. Ace-to-five low: wheel (5-4-3-2-A) is the nuts.
strategy.advanced: Strategic folding to deny an opponent the board card they need. Represent strength by betting when your board looks weak. Pot limit amplifies implied odds.
tips: Your board cards are public; assume at least one will be used against you.
Who acts first in second and third rounds is determined by highest board (pairs/trips).
You cannot fold if you have already matched the current bet.

scoring.description: Pot is won by the player with the lowest five-card hand at showdown (ace-to-five ranking), or by the last player when all others fold. Ties split the pot.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest hand at showdown wins the pot; ace-to-five low ranking.

synthesis.shortDescription: Lowball variant of Swingo Poker. Five cards each; choose two hole and three board. Lowest five-card hand (ace-to-five) from seven cards wins. Pot limit.
